Depression. As discussed on p.373 there is very little differ- ence in efficacy between the different groups of antidepressant drugs, and choice is often made on the basis of adverse effects. The traditional MAOIs such as phenelzine are rarely used as first-choice antidepressants because of the dangers of dietary and drug interactions. Reversible inhibitors of monoamine oxidase type A (RIMAs) such as moclobemide offer a safer alternative to the irreversible non-selective MAOIs and fewer dietary restric- tions are necessary.
